english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for badly messing up a performance, work, or reputation.
Use this colloquial choice when you mean actively ruining or spoiling something.
Use this colloquial verb when something causes a situation or relationship to become much worse.
Use this when mess up means to spoil or ruin the result, situation, or relationship.

examples.english: Talking like that will butcher the company's reputation.
examples.traditional: 你咁樣講，會搞衰間公司個名。
examples.jyutping: nei5 gam2 joeng2 gong2 wui5 gaau2 seoi1 gaan1 gung1 si1 go3 meng2

examples.english: Changing things randomly like that will blight the whole project.
examples.traditional: 你咁樣亂咁改，直頭搞衰晒成件事。
examples.jyutping: nei5 gam2 joeng2 lyun6 gam3 goi2 zik6 tau4 gaau2 seoi1 saai3 seng4 gin6 si6

examples.english: Doing this will poison the whole situation.
examples.traditional: 你咁樣做會搞衰晒成件事喎。
examples.jyutping: nei5 gam3 joeng2 zou6 wui5 gaau2 seoi1 saai3 sing4 gin6 si6 wo3

examples.english: If you do it like that, you will mess the whole thing up.
examples.traditional: 你咁樣做會搞衰成件事。
